tagline: Reddit is a community of communities
hero_kpi_rationale: Daily Active Uniques is the physical anchor of the Reddit model: published every quarter without interruption since the March 2024 listing, comparable across social platforms, and directly tied to advertising monetisation. The series covers fourteen quarters, from Q1 2023 to Q2 2026, rebuilt from the comparative figures in the company's quarterly earnings releases.

kpis.name: Daily Active Uniques (DAUq)
kpis.explanation: Average number of distinct daily visitors over the quarter, logged in or not.
kpis.description: Fourteen consecutive quarters of growth, from 60.3 million in Q1 2023 to 130.3 million in Q2 2026.
kpis.signal: 130.3 million daily active uniques in Q2 2026, up 18% year over year.

kpis.name: Weekly Active Uniques (WAUq)
kpis.explanation: Average number of distinct weekly visitors over the quarter.
kpis.description: Weekly reach crossed half a billion in Q2 2026, a base four times wider than the daily audience.
kpis.signal: 514.6 million weekly active uniques in Q2 2026, up 24% year over year.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total quarterly revenue, advertising plus content licensing.
kpis.description: Eight consecutive quarters of growth above 60%.
kpis.signal: Revenue of $804.9 million in Q2 2026, up 61% year over year.

kpis.name: Net income
kpis.explanation: Quarterly net income attributable to the company.
kpis.description: Profitable every quarter since Q3 2024, after losses from inception.
kpis.signal: Net income of $252.8 million in Q2 2026, 31% of revenue, more than double a year earlier.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortisation and share-based compensation, as defined by the company.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin widened from 33.4% to 42.6% in one year.
kpis.signal: Adjusted EBITDA of $342.8 million in Q2 2026, 43% of revenue, up 106% year over year.

kpis.name: Advertising revenue
kpis.explanation: Quarterly revenue from advertising sold on the platform.
kpis.description: Advertising still accounts for nearly 95% of revenue.
kpis.signal: Advertising revenue of $761.6 million in Q2 2026, up 64% year over year.

kpis.name: Other revenue (data licensing)
kpis.explanation: Quarterly revenue outside advertising, essentially content licensing for AI model training.
kpis.description: A second revenue line that did not exist before 2024: $3.7 million in Q1 2023 against $43.3 million in Q2 2026.
kpis.signal: Other revenue of $43.3 million in Q2 2026, up 24% year over year.

kpis.name: Average revenue per unique (ARPU)
kpis.explanation: Quarterly revenue divided by average daily active uniques over the same quarter, as defined by the company.
kpis.description: Monetisation per user is growing faster than the audience itself.
kpis.signal: ARPU of $6.18 in Q2 2026, up 36% year over year: $11.85 in the United States against $2.26 in the rest of the world.

kpis.name: Annual revenue
kpis.description: Revenue has more than tripled in three years.
kpis.signal: $2.20 billion in 2025, after $1.30 billion in 2024 and $0.80 billion in 2023.

kpis.name: Annual advertising revenue
kpis.signal: $2,062 million of advertising revenue in 2025, up 74% year over year.

kpis.name: Annual other revenue
kpis.description: Ten times the 2023 level, reflecting the content licensing agreements signed in 2024.

kpis.name: Revenue outside the United States
kpis.explanation: Full-year revenue billed outside the United States.
kpis.description: The international share is growing faster than the home market.
kpis.signal: $417.0 million outside the United States in 2025, up 76%, 18.9% of revenue.

risks.title: User base growth and retention
risks.description: Reddit faces intense competition. Failing to grow or retain its daily active uniques, or to sustain engagement, would hurt its results and financial position.
risks.score_rationale: First risk in the risk factor chapter of the company's 2025 annual report, direct wording ("We face intense competition"), trend stable against the prior year, market category weighted high because it underpins the advertising model.

risks.title: Managing growth and company culture
risks.description: Rapid headcount and organisational growth may outpace the company's processes and dilute the culture that underpins its product decisions.
risks.score_rationale: Risk located in the operations part of the chapter, moderate wording, trend stable, organisational category weighted medium.

risks.title: Security breaches and data security incidents
risks.description: A breach of security measures or an attack on systems holding personal data would damage the platform's perceived reliability and drive users and advertisers away.
risks.score_rationale: Thirteenth of the eighteen risks summarised at the head of the chapter, explicit wording on loss of user and advertiser trust, trend stable, cyber category weighted high by construction.

risks.title: Growing complexity of content and privacy regulation
risks.description: The company is subject to increasingly dense and changing rules on content, consumer protection, competition and privacy, in several jurisdictions at once.
risks.score_rationale: Fifteenth of the eighteen risks summarised at the head of the chapter, wording pointing to increasing complexity, trend up as texts multiply, regulatory category weighted high.

risks.title: Changing tax regimes across jurisdictions
risks.description: Changes in tax rules in the countries where the company operates could raise its effective tax rate or create additional liabilities.
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed in the later part of the chapter, conditional wording, trend stable, tax category weighted medium.

risks.title: Volatility of the Class A share price
risks.description: Interest from retail investors, for reasons unrelated to the business, can drive sharp swings in the Class A share price.
risks.score_rationale: Sixteenth of the eighteen risks summarised at the head of the chapter, wording explicitly citing reasons unrelated to the underlying business, trend stable, market category weighted medium as it does not affect operations.

risks.title: Dependence on search engine referral
risks.description: Part of Reddit's traffic comes from organic search, mainly through Google. An algorithm change that lowered the ranking of its pages would cut visitor numbers, hence the monetisable audience and advertising revenue.
risks.score_rationale: Fourth of the eighteen risks summarised at the head of the chapter of the company's 2025 annual report. Broad wording: the document states traffic and ultimately the business could be adversely affected, and names Google as the source of organic traffic. Trend stable, wording carried over unchanged. Market category weighted high because logged-out traffic feeds the daily audience that serves as the advertising base.

risks.title: Content licensing concentrated on two partners
risks.description: Revenue outside advertising rests on content licensing agreements for AI model training. The company states that substantially all of the contract value comes from two partners only, under medium-term contracts that may not be renewed or may be renewed on less favourable terms.
risks.score_rationale: Tenth of the eighteen risks summarised at the head of the chapter of the company's 2025 annual report. Explicit and quantified wording: substantially all of the contract value of licensing revenue comes from two partners, and the model is described as novel without an established track record. Trend up: this line grew from $15.2 million in 2023 to $140.0 million in 2025. Business model category weighted high because it is the only meaningful revenue source outside advertising.

ai_positioning.summary: Reddit monetises its conversational data through content licensing agreements with AI companies, while using internally built models to improve its own products. It does not develop a foundation model of its own.
evidence: We use internally built and trained models to improve many aspects of Reddit. Reddit Community Intelligence blends AI-driven efficiency with real user perspectives, enabling Reddit Insights, an AI-powered social listening tool, and Conversation Summary Add-ons.
Machine learning models are used for contextual keyword audience reach and interest-based audience reach, ranking ads on brand suitability and predicted user engagement.
Machine learning-powered auto-bidding (Maximum Clicks, Maximum Conversions) helps advertisers maximise campaign objectives and return on investment.
In January 2026 the company introduced a beta version of Max campaigns, an automated campaign type enabled by Reddit Community Intelligence that predicts the value of every ad impression.

Substantially all of the contract value associated with licensing revenue is derived from two partners: content licensing for AI training is a real but concentrated second revenue line ($140.0 million in 2025).
